description: Fact sheet for the elements with no measured excited atomic level: Md (101), Lr (103), Rf-Og (104-118). Not an element file of the SCHEMA.md kind (no NIST level to attach data to); compute.py does not read it.

status_no_measured_levels.statement: As of June 2026 no excited level of the neutral atom has been measured by optical or laser spectroscopy for any of these 17 elements. The heaviest element with measured atomic levels is nobelium (Z = 102); for lawrencium the GSI laser search has so far found no transition.

sources.source: E. Rickert et al., Eur. Phys. J. D 80, 88 (2026), abstract and p. 1-2: 'The heaviest chemical element for which atomic levels were experimentally determined to date is nobelium'; p. 9: 'did not reveal a clear indication of a transition'

S.-M. Udrescu, A. Belley, J.D. Holt et al., 'Probing the electroweak structure of nuclei with rare atoms and molecules', arXiv:2608.18219 (2026), p. 38: 'establishing nobelium as the heaviest element studied by optical spectroscopy'
J. Li, V. Dzuba, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 247, 106943 (2020), arXiv:2002.08033v1, p. 2 (Md: no measurements)

what_has_been_measured.text: The first ionisation potential, by surface ionisation of 256Lr atoms one at a time (4.96 +0.05/-0.04 eV), and a lower limit of 13.0 eV for the second ionisation potential from a charge-exchange reaction (second-hand, Kwarsick et al., cited by Rickert et al.). A laser search at GSI (two-step resonance ionisation of 255Lr, about 1500 cm-1 scanned in total around the transitions predicted near 20 300 and 28 600 cm-1) found no atomic transition.

conflicts: Md ionisation energy: measured 6.59(13) eV (Sato 2018) vs NIST [6.58(7)] eV, which is Sugar's 1974 semi-empirical value, not a measurement; they agree. The measured value is the entry.
Lr ionisation energy: 4.96 +0.08/-0.07 eV (Sato 2015) vs 4.96 +0.05/-0.04 eV (Sato 2018, weighted average of both runs, adopted by NIST as 4.96(5)). The 2018 value is the entry.

Db, Sg, Bh, Hs ionisation energy: NIST theoretical values 6.8(5), 7.8(5), 7.7(5), 7.6(5) eV vs CIPT calculations 7.01, 8.22, 8.03, 8.52 eV (Lackenby et al. 2019) vs the Smits et al. review table 6.814, 7.7, 8.6, 9.5 eV. All are calculations; NIST is the entry, the others are alternatives. For Hs the spread reaches 1.9 eV.

Ds, Rg, Cn ionisation energy: CIPT 10.158, 11.175, 12.145 eV (derived from cm-1, Lackenby et al. 2020) vs the review table 9.562, 11.03, 12.02 eV; the review says CIPT overestimates the late 6d elements. The CIPT value is the entry only because that paper was opened; the review values are second-hand.
Db ionisation limit in Lackenby et al. 2018: 56744 cm-1 in the text, 56733 cm-1 in Table II.

Lr predicted 7s2 8s 2S1/2 level: 20485 cm-1 (CI+MBPT) and 20533(303) cm-1 (coupled cluster) in Kahl et al. 2021; Rickert et al. 2026 quote a newer multiconfiguration calculation (Andrews et al., arXiv:2505.15121, not opened) that moves the two search lines to 20736 and 28607 cm-1.
Cn 6d10 7s7p 3P*1 level: 47293 cm-1 (Lackenby et al. 2020) vs 53144 / 55057 cm-1 (Dinh et al. 2008, methods B / A).

Sg, Bh, Hs, Mt ionisation energy in the Smits et al. review table (7.7, 8.6, 9.5, 10.4 eV) equals the 'RHF' column of Lackenby et al. 2019 Table VIII (7.70, 8.63, 9.52, 10.4 eV, from Dzuba 2016), not the CIPT column (8.22, 8.03, 8.52, 9.86 eV) of the same table; both are calculations.
not_found: Sato et al., Nature 520, 209 (2015) full text: the CERN repository preprint is behind a bot check and its archived copy is the check page; only the abstract (Europe PMC) was read.
Transition rates for Rf I, Cn I, Nh I, Fl I, Mc I: the opened papers give level energies only; 'predicted_lines' for these elements are E1-allowed levels, not ranked by strength.
Fl: only two E1-allowed (J = 1 odd) levels are listed in the opened table.
Original papers behind the Smits et al. review table (Borschevsky 2015 for Mc, Lv, Ts; Kaygorodov 2022 for Rg, Cn, Nh, Fl; Arbely thesis for Db, Ds) were not opened.
Original papers behind the NIST values for Db (Dolg 1993), Sg (Johnson 1999), Bh, Hs (Johnson 2002) and Md (Sugar 1974) were not opened; the numbers are as NIST prints them.
The specific compounds used in Bh and Hs gas-phase chemistry, and the Cn adsorption enthalpy on gold, were not read in an opened source.
Half-lives newer than NUBASE2020 (several heaviest isotopes have been remeasured since) were not collected.
notes: All ionisation energies except Md and Lr are calculations (method 'theory'); entries with method 'compilation' under 'alternatives' are also calculated values, read second-hand in a review. Ground configurations and terms are calculated for every element here except Md (as listed by NIST). 'predicted_lines' are theory throughout; A_s is the calculated Einstein coefficient of that line. Values with 'value_cm' were printed in cm-1 and converted to eV here (derived). Lr uncertainties are asymmetric (unc_plus / unc_minus). Half-lives are from NUBASE2020; where NUBASE lists a longer but poorly known isotope or isomer it is given under 'alternative'. Verification pass 2026-10-02: every number was re-read in its source; for Md the two strong ground-state lines to J = 9/2 levels (347.27 nm, 484.33 nm) were added, so Md lists five predicted lines ordered by A.
